object_description: three separate elongated buildings around a central square
design_condition: The school, kindergarten and sports hall are separated into three aligned volumes that form a central break area, with the square slightly sunken from the street and the buildings independently addressing access, parking and the surrounding neighborhood.

positive.statement: The three buildings form an identity-forming center through which the school complex radiates into the district.
The school complex offers a clever solution to the situation.
The three volumes create exciting spatial sequences inside and outside.
The kindergarten's western playground and overall quality should be emphasized.
The facades create an attractive and appropriate external appearance.
The project demonstrates design care and an intensive examination of user needs.
The proposed lightweight construction has good ecological values.

negative.statement: There is no traffic-safe waiting and play area at the kindergarten access, and a larger covered area and vestibule are desirable.
The sports-hall cloakrooms are reached through the spectator stands or a narrow escape staircase, and their connection to the outdoor field is not optimal.
The classrooms are arranged on one side of the corridor, which is seen as a disadvantage from a school perspective.
The classrooms only have windows on one side.
The dazzling effect of the light strips must be reduced with appropriate measures.
The kindergarten common area could be more spacious and spatially upgraded.
The lightweight construction's acoustic measures and effective activation of storage mass are questionable.
The classroom-wide windows and cloakroom air spaces limit long-term flexibility and management potential.
The three functional areas can only be reached by walking distance, which is a disadvantage in everyday use.
